what_its_for: Fludrocortisone is used to replace a hormone that your body does not make enough of on its own. It is most commonly used to treat Addison's disease (where your adrenal glands do not work properly) and a condition called salt-wasting syndrome. It helps your body hold onto the right amount of salt and water to keep your blood pressure at a healthy level.
how_to_take: Take fludrocortisone by mouth, with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with a meal or snack. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can cause serious problems.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 0.1 mg (one tablet) taken once a day, but your doctor may adjust your dose based on how you feel and your lab results. Some people may need as little as 0.05 mg or as much as 0.2 mg per day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose. Your dose may need to be increased during times of stress, illness, surgery, or extreme heat.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on that same day. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you miss several doses in a row, contact your doctor right away.
storage: Store fludrocortisone at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it in a dry place away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medication in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating a high-potassium diet or taking potassium supplements unless your doctor tells you to, as this medication affects your body's potassium levels. Avoid consuming large amounts of licorice, as it can increase the effects of this medication. Limit alcohol, as it may increase the risk of stomach problems. Avoid contact with people who are sick or have infections, as fludrocortisone can weaken your immune system. Be careful in very hot weather or during intense exercise, and make sure to stay well hydrated. Avoid stopping this medication suddenly without your doctor's guidance.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: swelling in your hands, feet, or ankles; rapid weight gain (more than 2 to 3 pounds in a day); muscle weakness or cramps; unusual tiredness or fatigue; headache, dizziness, or fainting; increased thirst or urination; vision changes; signs of infection such as fever or chills; chest pain or irregular heartbeat; mood changes, confusion, or depression; or if you feel worse than usual or cannot keep your medication down due to vomiting. Go to the emergency room immediately if you have signs of a serious adrenal crisis such as severe nausea, vomiting, extreme weakness, or loss of consciousness.
when_it_works: Fludrocortisone starts working within a few hours of your first dose to help balance your salt and water levels. However, it may take a few days to several weeks for you to feel the full benefit and for your blood pressure and energy levels to stabilize. You will likely need to take this medication for the rest of your life if you have Addison's disease or a chronic hormone deficiency. Regular blood tests and blood pressure checks will help your doctor make sure it is working correctly.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before taking this medication if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. It may be necessary to continue treatment during pregnancy for your health, but your doctor will monitor you closely. Children: This medication can be used in children, but the dose will be adjusted by weight. It may affect a child's growth, so regular check-ups are important. Older adults: Older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medication, especially swelling, high blood pressure, and bone loss. Regular monitoring is especially important. Kidney or liver disease: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
